nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration sandbox / transaction fees during testing
Cloud infra for staging/CI environment (3 months)
Contingency for third-party services (email, search, FX rate feed)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; hour estimates are derived from story points using an assumed velocity of ~6-7 hours of blended effort per point, not from past delivery data.
1 story point ≈ 6.5 hours of combined team effort, split across roles based on task type (backend-heavy, frontend-heavy, QA/DevOps-heavy).

Backend Developer capacity is 1.5 FTE (~240 hrs/month); allocated 900 hours implies ~3.75 months of full backend capacity, which is tight given backend involvement in nearly every backlog item (auth, RBAC, payments, migration, audit, search) — this role is staffed thinly relative to backlog demand and may need contracting support or schedule extension.
Frontend Developer is a single 1.0 FTE; 620 hours (~3.9 months) assumes near-full dedication, leaving little slack for rework or parallel design-system iteration.
QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE (620 hours 4-month equivalent) is proportionate only if testing is concentrated on Urgent/High items and lighter on Low-priority items.
DevOps Engineer at 0.4 FTE is assumed sufficient given DevOps effort is concentrated in CI/staging setup, observability, and legacy decommission, not continuous full-time work.

Legacy data migration (PW-8) is assumed to require a data migration tool/license and dedicated backend hours; actual legacy schema complexity could increase this significantly — flagged as a major cost risk.
Non-labour costs are rough placeholder estimates for third-party services (Stripe fees, cloud hosting, migration tooling, accessibility audit, contingency) since no vendor quotes were provided.
Scenario percentiles reflect uncertainty mainly driven by legacy migration complexity, RBAC/permission matrix scope, and multi-currency settlement logic, which are the least well-defined items.
Low-priority items (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24) are included in the Most Likely estimate but are the first candidates for descoping if budget is constrained.
input.reasoning: Effort was sized bottom-up from the 24 backlog items' story points, converting points to hours via an assumed blended velocity (~6.5 hrs/point), then allocating those hours across the four staffed roles according to each task's nature (e.g., PW-8 legacy migration and PW-4 RBAC are backend-heavy; PW-2 design system and PW-15 accessibility are frontend-heavy; PW-1 CI/staging and PW-22 observability are DevOps-heavy; all items carry a QA testing allocation proportional to complexity). Total story points = 189, translating to roughly 1,000 hours of blended effort before role-specific weighting, but role allocations were adjusted so hours stay within realistic FTE capacity ratios (Backend 1.5 FTE, Frontend 1.0 FTE, QA 0.6 FTE, DevOps 0.4 FTE) over an assumed ~4-month delivery window. This produced 900 Backend, 620 Frontend, 330 QA, and 150 DevOps hours. Non-labour costs cover third-party services directly implied by the backlog (Stripe fees, staging cloud infra, migration tooling, accessibility audit, and a contingency buffer for ancillary services like email/search/FX feeds). The Most Likely scenario equals the sum of all line items (192,897 USD). Optimistic (-12%) assumes fewer integration surprises and lower migration overhead; Pessimistic (+19%) reflects the well-known risk that legacy data migration, RBAC enforcement across API+UI, and multi-currency settlement often overrun estimates, plus the backend role's thin staffing ratio relative to backlog demand. Priority breakdown allocates each backlog item's estimated cost bucket by its stated priority label. No historical actuals exist for this project, so all effort ratios are assumption-based rather than derived from past delivery data, as noted in the assumptions list.

reductions.description: Descope Admin back-office for support staff (PW-18, Low priority, 13 points) to a later phase
reductions.effect: Removes an entire feature from this delivery cycle; support staff continue using existing manual/DB-level tooling until phase 2.

reductions.description: Defer Usage analytics and reporting (PW-19, Low, 8 points) and Contract tests against helpdesk API (PW-23, Low, 5 points)
reductions.effect: Both are low-priority and not required for launch; can be delivered post-launch without blocking customer-facing functionality.

reductions.description: Reduce QA hours on Low-priority items (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24) to smoke-test level only instead of full test cycles
reductions.effect: Lower QA depth on low-risk, low-priority features; slightly higher escaped-defect risk on those specific items only.

reductions.description: Defer the third-party accessibility audit (non-labour) and rely on internal WCAG checklist review for the first release
reductions.effect: Removes external audit cost from this phase; formal audit can be scheduled after initial launch feedback.

reductions.description: Simplify Multi-currency support (PW-14) to launch with USD+EUR only, deferring PLN support
reductions.effect: Reduces backend and QA effort for FX handling and settlement logic by roughly a third; PLN added in a follow-up release.
